newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Mandela and companion Graca meet Swedish royals.
newsitem.headline: Mandela and companion Graca meet Swedish royals.

text.p: South African President Nelson Mandela rekindled talk on Tuesday that he might remarry when he appeared hand-in-hand with his Mozambican sweetheart Graca Machel to meet King Carl Gustaf and Queen Silvia of Sweden.
The king was welcomed by a 21-gun salute outside the Cape Town parliament to which Mandela and his African National Congress brought democracy in 1994.

Mandela and Gustaf exchanged medals and met privately for 40 minutes at the start of a three-day royal visit that includes talks with Archbishop Desmond Tutu, who heads the post-apartheid Truth and Reconciliation Commission.
Mandela, 78, last year confirmed his romance with Graca, 51-year-old widow of former Mozambican president Samora Machel, and said they would try to spend two weeks a month together.
The couple have appeared in public together in South Africa only twice before and never at a state function.
"This is the first time Mrs Machel has appeared with the President at a state function, but they will be appearing together a lot more in future," said an official in his office.
The media programme for King Carl's three-day state visit had referred only to "President Mandela and his companion".
Reporters had expected the president to be accompanied as usual by one of his daughters, Zindzi or Zenani, or by his closest granddaughter, Rochelle.
But as Mandela led the king down the steps of his office for a now traditional chat with tourists and pedestrians at the garden gate, it was Machel who came down with Queen Silvia.
At the gates, Mandela introduced the Swedish royal couple to onlookers and then took his companion by the hand.
"This is Mrs Machel," he said without further explanation in what was effectively her first introduction to the South African public.

Mandela's staff routinely decline to comment on his personal life, but a source in his office said Machel would accompany Mandela on a foreign visit for the first time next month, when he travels to southeast Asia.
Mandela divorced his wife of 38 years, Winnie, 11 months ago after a court battle in which he was forced to reveal bedroom secrets and to acknowledge that she had been unfaithful to him.
His first wife, Evelyn, lives in the rural southcoast Transkei, where he has built a retirement home.
Mandela has vowed not to seek reelection in South Africa's second democratic election in 1999. He says he has no plans to marry Machel but church leaders such as Tutu have urged him to do so.
